Subraveti, S.G., Rodríguez Angel, E., Ramírez, A. and Roussanaly, S. (2023). Is Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) Really So Expensive? An Analysis of Cascading Costs and CO2 Emissions Reduction of Industrial CCS Implementation on the Construction of a Bridge. Environmental Science & Technology 57(6), 2595-2601. doi:10.1021/acs.est.2c05724

Value-chain (cascading cost) study: CCS in cement (1.36 Mt/y dry kiln, oxy-fuel capture, 90% avoided) and steel (4 Mt HRC/y blast-furnace route, MDEA/Pz capture on the oxyfuel blast furnace, 94% capture rate, 47% of site emissions avoided) and the effect on the cost and CO2 of building the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway (EUR2018). Results are product-chain percentages: cement production cost +60%, HRC +13%, concrete +8%, steel products +10%, bridge cost 379 -> 382 MEUR (+1%), bridge CO2 130 -> 64 kt (-51%); bridge material quantities 76,487 t cement and 24,209 t steel; grid factor 262 kg CO2/MWh. The plant-level technology data are reprinted from CEMCAP (Voldsund et al. 2019 / Gardarsdottir et al. 2019) and IEAGHG 2013-04 (both already held and extracted) and the detailed numbers are in the Supporting Information, which is not held. No new technology-level numbers, so nothing extracted. No to-get.csv row found for this paper.
